title: The Conjuring 2
tagline: Shepherd's pie for four. Set a fifth place for the old man in the chair.
about: In 1977, paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren travel to north London to help a single mother whose council house has turned against her family.
cue: Serve the snacks when Janet and Margaret play with their homemade spirit board under the bedcovers.
faces: Shepherd's pie for four. Set a fifth place for the old man in the chair.
Kids, tea is at six. Nobody sits in that armchair, nobody touches the telly, and if the toy fire engine rolls down the hall on its own, you leave it alone and come to me.
Serve the snacks when Janet and Margaret play with their homemade spirit board under the bedcovers.
Prices subject to change. Printed offset at the counter. Form DS-1977.
Read it. Eat it. Fold it.

PEGGY HODGSON'S SAUSAGE ROLLS WITH BROWN SAUCE
Flaky puff pastry rolls of pork sausage, onion and sage, brushed with egg and baked golden.
BILL WILKINS'S ARMCHAIR CHEESE AND PICKLE TOASTIES
Buttered white bread fried golden around vintage cheddar, brown pickle and a smear of hot mustard.
Ed's guitar out, Elvis for the Hodgson kids.
Lamb mince braised with carrot, celery and thyme, peas through it.
MAURICE GROSSE'S FRIDAY FISH AND CHIPS
Maurice, the investigator with the tape recorder, brings tea home wrapped in newspaper.
JANET'S SCHOOL JAM ROLY-POLY WITH CUSTARD
Soft butter pudding dough rolled around raspberry jam and steam-baked.
Whisky with honey and lemon topped with boiling water, a clove-studded lemon slice and cinnamon.
Janet's mug, before the fire engine rolls.

ALSO IN THIS EDITION: The toy fire engine rolling down the hall. The old armchair in the front room. Ed's painting of the nun. The Crooked Man and his spinning toy. A tape recorder left running all night.

    StartersPeggy Hodgson's sausage rolls with brown sauceFlaky puff pastry rolls of pork sausage, onion and sage, brushed with egg and baked golden, with brown sauceHow to make it500g pork sausage mince1 brown onion, finely chopped1 tsp dried sage1/2 tsp white pepper2 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beaten125ml brown sauceHeat the oven to 200°C and line a tray. Mix the sausage mince with the onion, sage and white pepper.Cut each pastry sheet in half, lay a log of filling along each strip, roll up and press the seam closed.Cut each roll into 4, put seam side down on the tray and brush with the egg.Bake until puffed and deep golden.Cool for 5 minutes and serve warm with the brown sauce.Bill Wilkins's armchair cheese and pickle toastiesButtered white bread fried golden around vintage cheddar, brown pickle and a smear of hot mustardHow to make it8 slices of white bread40g butter, softened2 tsp hot English mustard200g vintage cheddar, grated4 tbsp brown pickleButter one side of each slice of bread.Turn 4 slices butter side down, spread thinly with mustard, pile on the cheddar and pickle and close with the other slices, butter side up.Fry in a frying pan over medium low heat, pressing with a spatula, for 4 minutes a side until golden and melted. Do it in two batches.Cut into triangles and serve hot.Pork pie with Branston pickleEd's guitar out, Elvis for the Hodgson kids.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsGreen Street shepherd's pieLamb mince braised with carrot, celery and thyme, peas through it, under buttery mash with a cheddar crustHow to make it1 tbsp vegetable oil1 brown onion, diced2 carrots, diced2 celery sticks, diced800g lamb mince2 tbsp tomato paste2 tbsp plain flour500ml beef stock1 tbsp worcestershire sauce1 tsp dried thyme150g frozen peassalt and pepper, to taste1.2kg floury potatoes, peeled and chunked60g butter100ml milk60g cheddar, gratedCook the onion, carrots and celery in the oil in a large pan over medium heat until soft.Turn up the heat, add the lamb mince and brown it well, breaking it up.Stir in the tomato paste and flour, then the stock, worcestershire and thyme. Simmer gently, stirring now and then, until thick.Meanwhile boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash with the butter and milk. Season with salt and pepper.Stir the peas through the mince, season and tip into a 2 litre baking dish. Heat the oven to 200°C.Spread the mash over the top, rough it up with a fork and scatter with the cheddar.Bake until the top is golden and the edges bubble.Rest for 5 minutes before serving.Maurice Grosse's Friday fish and chipsMaurice, the investigator with the tape recorder, brings tea home wrapped in newspaperHow to make it600g flathead fillets150g plain flour250ml cold lager1 tsp baking powder1 L vegetable oil1kg frozen thick chips400g frozen peas20g butter1 mint150g mayonnaise2 tbsp capers1 lemonmalt vinegar, to serveBake the chips at 220°C for 25 minutes.Cook the peas for 4 minutes, drain and crush with the butter, chopped mint and salt.Mix the mayonnaise with the chopped capers and a squeeze of lemon.Whisk 120g of the flour with the baking powder and lager until smooth.Heat the oil to 180°C. Dust the fish in the rest of the flour, dip in the batter and fry in batches for 4 minutes until golden.Serve with the chips, mushy peas, tartare, lemon and malt vinegar.SweetsJanet's school jam roly-poly with custardSoft butter pudding dough rolled around raspberry jam and steam-baked, sliced thick under hot vanilla custardHow to make it250g self-raising flour125g cold butter, grated2 tbsp caster sugar, for the doughpinch of salt150ml milk, for the dough150g raspberry jam500ml milk, for the custard4 egg yolks60g caster sugar, for the custard1 tbsp cornflour1 tsp vanilla extractHeat the oven to 180°C. Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and salt, then stir in the milk for the dough to make a soft dough.Roll out on a floured bench to 30cm by 20cm, spread with the jam leaving a 2cm border, roll up from a short side and pinch the ends closed.Wrap loosely in buttered baking paper, then foil, and sit it on a rack over a roasting tin half full of boiling water.Bake until risen and firm.Meanwhile heat the milk for the custard. Whisk the yolks, custard sugar and cornflour, pour on the hot milk, return to the pan and stir over low heat until thick, then add the vanilla.Rest the pudding for 5 minutes, slice thickly and serve with the hot custard.DrinksEnfield night watch hot toddyWhisky with honey and lemon topped with boiling water, a clove-studded lemon slice and cinnamonHow to make it160ml whisky3 tbsp honey1 lemon, half juiced and half cut into 4 slices8 cloves1 cinnamon stick600ml boiling waterPress 2 cloves into each lemon slice.Divide the honey, lemon juice and whisky between 4 heatproof glasses.Top with the boiling water, stir, add a lemon slice and a piece of cinnamon stick to each and steep for a few minutes.Serve hot.Hot RibenaJanet's mug, before the fire engine rolls.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
